title: mlflow traces search --order-by rejects entries with spaces after commas
answers: mlflow traces search order-by fails with 'Invalid order_by clause' when I add a space after the comma
sort traces by two fields from the CLI with a space after the comma does not work
traces search --order-by 'timestamp_ms DESC, status' errors out
CLI order by trace search could not be parsed leading whitespace
body:
Symptom: Running `mlflow traces search --order-by "timestamp_ms DESC, status"` fails with "Invalid order_by clause ' status'. Could not be parsed.", even though the help example uses that exact form.
Root cause: mlflow/cli/traces.py:search_traces splits the --order-by value on "," without stripping each entry. The leading space reaches the sqlparse-based order-by parser, which rejects any leading or trailing whitespace.
Fix pattern: Normalize each user-supplied comma-separated entry before passing it on, e.g. `[o.strip() for o in order_by.split(",")]`, the same way `mlflow datasets search` already handles its order-by option. Do this at the CLI boundary rather than loosening the downstream parser.
Constraints: Applies to any CLI option that takes a comma-separated list passed to a strict parser. Stripping only trims whitespace around entries; it does not change the parser's validation of field names or DESC/ASC tokens. Test with a space after the comma, e.g. in tests/cli/test_traces.py:test_search_command_strips_spaces_in_order_by.
applies: CLI comma-separated list options for trace search; new list-valued CLI options should strip entries the same way.
says: Sorting traces by multiple fields fails when including a space after the comma.
Searching traces with multiple sort options gives an invalid clause syntax error.
The command line trace search rejects standard multi-field sort arguments containing whitespace.
Allow spaces after commas when sorting trace search results by several columns.
search: In mlflow/cli/traces.py:search_traces, comma-separated entries in `--order-by` must be stripped of whitespace before reaching the sqlparse-based parser. Unstripped leading spaces cause the parser to reject the clause as invalid, whereas stripping normalizes entries at the CLI boundary similar to `mlflow datasets search`. Stripping only trims surrounding whitespace without loosening parser validation of field names or DESC and ASC tokens, as tested in tests/cli/test_traces.py:test_search_command_strips_spaces_in_order_by.
